full_judgment:
2. The suit was filed by the respondents and their father Mirza Murshal Hossain against the defendant-appellant for his ejectment and for realisation of arrear rent. The plaintiffs' case, inter alia, is that Mirza Murshal Hossain and his wife Begum Shamsun Nahar, inducted the defendant in the disputed premises under an agreement dated 14.8.69 with effect from 1.8.69 at a monthly rental of Taka 135.00 as per English Calendar month and subsequently the said Begum Shamsun Nahar died on 17.1.83, leaving husband Mirza Murshal Hossain and a son and a daughter, the respondents; that the defendant is a defaulter and he has defaulted to pay rents of the disputed premises from September1975; that the plaintiffs required the suit premises for construction of the undone part of their multi-storied building, construction of new gas, water and sewerage lines and for keeping a passage for going to and coming from the back staircase of the building and that after serving notice upon the defendant under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, on 16.6.84 terminated the tenancy and claimed eviction of the defendant along with the recovery of arrear rents of Taka 4,860.00. 

 3. The defendant by filing a written statement denied that he is a defaulter and the premises is required for reconstruction and for taking new gas, sewerage, water lines and for keeping passage in the back staircase. The defendant's positive case, inter alia, is that he paid Taka 3,500.00 as advance and the rent was payable in advance on or before the 10th day of each month and in default the defendant should bear interest at the rate of 50% per annum upon the rent; that the defendant has been running his business of confectionery, tea, milk, etc.; that plaintiff No.1 took rents from the defendant and he confirmed that payment of rent upto June, 1977 by granting a receipt on 4.7.77; that plaintiff No. 1 from 3.7.77 to 31.5.78 bought milk on credit worth Taka 1203.00 and plaintiff No. 1 promised to adjust the same with the rent of the disputed premises; that plaintiff No.1 during the construction work of extension of the disputed holding took an advance of Taka 17,500.00 from the defendant by cheque and also in cash with a promise to allot another shop in the holding after the completion of the construction work and in default to allot another shop to the defendant the aforesaid advance of Taka 17,500.00 would be treated as an advance rent of the disputed premises; that plaintiff No. 1 agreed in writing for adjustment of the aforesaid amount; that since July 1977 upto the month of December, 1984 the total rent for 90 months at the rate of Taka 135.00 per month would be Taka 12,150.00 and the remaining Taka 10,053.00 would be at the hands of the plaintiffs which could easily be adjusted towards the rents of the disputed premises for some more years would be treated as an advance rent of the disputed premises; that plaintiff No.1 agreed in writing for adjustment of the aforesaid amount; that since July 1977 upto the month of December, 1984 the total rent for 90 months at the rate of Taka 135.00 per month would be Taka 12,150.00 and the remaining Taka 10,053.00 would be at the hands of the plaintiffs which could easily be adjusted towards the rents of the disputed premises for some more years with effect from 1.1.85 and accordingly, the defendant is not a defaulter from September, 1975 and the question of construction as claimed in the plaint does not arise: that the defendant on 22.4.89 by filing an additional written statement disclosed that the aforesaid amount was adjusted upto the month of December 1988 and then there was balance of advance money of Taka 70.00 with the plaintiffs and the defendant sent the rent through money order and after refusal of the same by the plaintiffs, he deposited rents to the Premises Rent Controller (4th Assistant Judge), Dhaka on 30.3.89 by filing House Rent Case No.12 of 1989 and since then he has been depositing the rents to the Court and the question of default does not arise at all. 

 4. The learned Subordinate Judge found on consideration of the materials on record, both oral and documentary, that the defendant paid rent upto August, 1975 and filed rent receipt of the same. The trial Court found that the defendant did not file any rent receipt in assertion of his claim of payment of rent from September, 1975. For non-filing of any rent receipt after August, 1975 the trial Court disbelieved the defendant's case of payment of rent from September, 1975. The trial Court on consideration of the documentary evidences found that the plaintiff, in fact, admitted the payment of money by the defendant. The trial Judge found that under section 13 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance the tenant is entitled to get rent receipt from the landlord and in the event of the failure of the landlord to grant rent-receipts to the tenant, the tenant can start a proceeding under section 27 of the Ordinance before the Rent Controller but in the present case the defendant took no such proceeding. The trial Judge further found that the plaintiff requires the premises for reconstruction of his multi-storied building and for setting up other utility services such as, installation of new gas, water, sewerage lines. On the the above findings the suit was decreed 

 6. Leave was granted to consider whether the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division acted wrongly in affirming the decision of the SCC Judge when the latter on misreading of the evidence both oral and documentary on record held that the defendant was a defaulter and that the plaintiffs required the suit premises for their bonafide requirements. Leave was also granted for considering the vital aspect of the case, that admittedly the plaintiffs had in their hands unadjusted amount of money paid by the defendant which could be easily adjusted towards the payment of rent and whether on these facts the defendant could be termed as a defaulter. 

 8. PW 1 Masud Hossain, son of plaintiff No. 1, deceased Mirza Murshal Hossain, deposed that the defendant did not pay any rent from September, 1975. He also denied the fact of defendant's paying rent upto June 1977. This witness admitted the acceptance of Taka 3,500.00 as security from the defendant. He denied the defendant's suggestion of adjustment of price of milk of Taka 1203.00 towards the rent. He admitted acceptance of Taka 17,500.00 from the defendant but denied the defendant's case of adjustment of the same towards rent. He further deposed that they required the shop premises for reconstruction of staircase, gas and sewerage lines. DW 1 Monoranjan Barua, the defendant filed the account book which was marked as Exhibit "Kha" and this witness proved the signature of plaintiff No. 1 Ext. Kha(1). He stated that Murshal Hossain (plaintiff No. 1) after acceptance of rent upto July 1977 has written the account book in his own hand. He also stated that from July 1977 upto 31.5.78 the plaintiff took milk on credit by coupon and wrote the same in his own hand in exhibit 'Kha', He also deposed that he paid Taka 17,500.00 to plaintiff No. 1 by cheques and cash with an agreement that in the event of plaintiffs failure to provide another shop room in the said market the amount will be adjusted towards the payment of rent and the same was written in the diary by the plaintiff himself after putting his signature. The defendant filed the said diary which is marked as Exhibit 'Gha', According to the testimony of DW 1, supply of milk of Taka 1203.00 on credit was agreed to be adjusted towards the payment of rent. He deposed that even after adjustment of rent upto February, 1989 there will be some more money in the hands of the plaintiffs. He also testified that the construction of first floor is completed and the second floor is about to be finished. According to this witness in the said holding there is a staircase, gas, water and sewerage lines from before 

 10. DW 4 Md. Raisuddin has a shop 10/15 cubits away from the disputed shop. He testified that on the eastern side of the disputed shop there is a staircase and on the top of the disputed shop first floor has been constructed. According to this witness, sewerage and water lines are already in existence. This is all the material oral evidence on record. Along with this oral evidence, we will mention about the documentary evidences produced in this case by the defendant. Exhibit 'Kha' is the account book which shows payment of rent upto June, 1977 and reads as follows: 

 "In this exhibit, we find several coupon numbers containing different dates (for supply of milk) with the signature of plaintiff No.1 by the side of each coupon. A reference to Ext. 'Gha' shows payment of Taka 17,500.00 by three cheques and by cash for allotment of a new shop room measuring 12' x 8' by the side of the existing disputed shop. There is a clear recital in the said Exhibit." From the documentary evidences particularly, Ext. "Kha" we find that rent upto June 1977 was paid and in Ext. "Kha" we find the signature of plaintiff No. 1 by the side of each coupon. From Ext "Gha" we also find that there has been a payment of Taka 17,500.00 to plaintiff No. 1 with a clear stipulation that the same will be treated as advance rent in the event of failure of the plaintiff to allot a new shop room. From these exhibits it is clear that money was already in the hands of the plaintiffs when the suit was filed. 

 11. Thus, the trial Judge on a misreading of the oral and documentary evidences on record and without considering the effect of those documents held the defendant to be a defaulter. The trial Judge also failed to notice another important aspect of the case that there is assertion in the plaint that the defendant is a defaulter from September, 1975, whereas from the admitted documents filed by the defendant and believed by the trial Court and the learned Single Judge rent was paid upto June, 1977. 

 12. Mr. Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff- respondents, submitted that in Ext. "Kha" account book, there is no signature of plaintiff No. 1 by the side of the writing 'rent paid upto June 1977' and hence the document is false. 

 14. Mr. Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed further argued that as no rent-receipt has been filed from September, 1975 nor any case has been filed by the defendant under section 27 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance for violation of section 13 of the said Ordinance the trial Court including the learned Single Judge rightly held that the defendant is a defaulter. He also cited the case of Mosammat Rahima Khatun vs. Abdur Rashid Bhuiyan and another reported in BCR 1984 (AD) 520. 

 15. Section 13 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance provides that a tenant who makes a payment of rent to the landlord is entitled to obtain rent receipt forthwith from the landlord. Section 27 of the Ordinance provides that if a landlord wilfully refuses or fails to deliver a receipt to the tenant in accordance with the provision of section 13, a tenant may file a complaint before the Rent Controller. Section 27 of the Ordinance provides for a penalty. In the present case no such proceeding was taken by the tenant under section 27 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance, because there was no wilful refusal or failure to deliver the rent receipt by the landlord as is evident from the oral and documentary evidences on record, DW 1 stated in his deposition that he has been regularly paying rent to the landlord and submitted those rent receipts granted by the landlord. He has further testified that the relationship with plaintiff No.1 was so cordial that at the time of realisation of rent he used to give receipts at times and at times he did not give any rent receipt. Exhibits "Kha'' and "Gha" are indicative of good relationship between the parties. Hence non-filing of the rent receipts by itself will not be so material as from the evidence on record admittedly the unadjusted amount remains in the hands of the plaintiffs. It may be mentioned here that the filing of the rent receipt in support of the claim of the defendant of payment of rent up to June, 1977 would have been the best evidence in the case but the defendant having actually proved the payment of rent by oral and documentary evidences the trial Court including the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division wrongly held the defendant to be a defaulter. 

 16. In the case of BCR 1984 (AD) 520, cited by Mr. Khandker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, this Division while considering the case of eviction of a tenant on the ground of default in payment of rent did not consider the question of adjustment of the rents for the months for which default has been made by the respondents against the security money deposited by them as no proceeding was taken under section 14 of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance within six months before the House Rent Controller. As no application under section 14 of the Ordinance was made praying for adjustment against the security money that question was not gone into. This Division further held in the case of Shamsuddin Ahmed vs. Mohd. Hassan and others, 31 DLR (AD) 155, has no application in the facts of the case. Hence this case is not very relevant for our purpose. 

 17. I will now consider the case cited by Mr. TH Khan to show that there being admitted unadjusted money in the hands of the plaintiffs the same could be adjusted towards the rent. 

 18. In the case of Shamsuddin Ahmed vs. Mohd. Hassan and others, 31 DLR (AD) 155, this Division while holding that taking of advance rent for more than one month as contemplated in section 10 of the Ordinance is illegal, observed that the tenant could not be said to be a defaulter in payment of rent within the meaning of section 18(5) of the Premises Rent Control Ordinance as long as the money in the hands of the plaintiff-landlord could be adjusted towards the payment of rent. In the present case we find that the amount of Taka 17,500.00 was not paid to the landlord in consideration of the grant, renewal or continuance of the tenancy and hence section 10 of the Ordinance is not attracted.
